notes.1a: Most candidates were able to explain the term with many being awarded both of the available marks.
notes.1b: There were many fully correct calculations and nearly all candidates were aware of the method to calculate the accumulated fund and there were no common errors.
notes.1c: The subscriptions account was prepared to a high standard with some candidates being awarded full marks. The common errors were the omission or incorrect treatment of the irrecoverable debt and the incorrect posting of the opening and/or closing balances.
notes.1d: The extract from the statement of financial position was well prepared by most candidates but a limited number of candidates did not to show the section headings.
notes.1e: Most candidates were able to identify two appropriate ways to increase the future annual surplus but only a limited number were able to develop their answer sufficiently to be awarded more than two of the available four marks.
notes.1f: Those candidates who were aware that the treatment was incorrect generally developed their answer appropriately with many being awarded all of the four available marks. The limited number who incorrectly stated that the treatment was correct generally showed little understanding of the topic.
notes.2a: (i) Although most candidates demonstrated knowledge of the term, relatively few provided an explanation worthy of two marks and consequently one mark was awarded to the vast majority of candidates.
notes.2aii: This was very well answered with nearly all of the candidates stating two correct duties of the auditor.
notes.2b: Many candidates prepared the extract correctly and there were no common errors. �PAGE�15
notes.2c: The statement of changes in equity was well prepared with some fully correct statements. The most common errors were the incorrect inclusion of the proposed dividend and the omission of the profit for the year.
notes.2d: The statement of financial position was also well prepared by most candidates. The most common error was the omission of the debenture interest accrual.
notes.2e: Although many candidates were able to correctly calculate both the fair value and value in use only a limited number calculated the impairment loss as was required.
notes.2f: Although some candidates did identify the relevant standards, the general discussion of the decision, with a few exceptions, was not satisfactory.
notes.3a: Although many candidates did correctly enter the current liabilities, relatively few were able to deduce the ordinary share capital and share premium and even fewer entered the retained earnings in the statement of financial position.
notes.3b: The calculations of the ratios were performed well with candidates being able to obtain the available marks for using their own figures correctly where errors had been made in part (a). Some candidates did not give their answers to two decimal places as was required.
notes.3c: The analysis of the financial performance was made to a reasonable standard although in some cases there was insufficient development.
notes.3d: The mark for the advice was generally awarded but the justification was often not worthy of credit with few candidates stating that there was insufficient cash to pay the proposed dividend without raising the additional funds.
notes.4a: Relatively few candidates were able to correctly calculate the gain on realisation due to errors in calculating the gain/loss of the assets and liabilities and the goodwill.
notes.4b: The capital accounts were well prepared with the most common error being the omission or incorrect treatment of the ordinary shares.
notes.4c: The statement of financial position was also well prepared. Common errors included omission of goodwill and / or not accounting correctly for the share premium.
notes.4d: Nearly all candidates stated at least one appropriate advantage whilst some did state two advantages and obtained both marks.
notes.4e: Most candidates did provide the required advice but many did not justify their advice. Some candidates did not support their answer with calculations.
notes.5a: This was well answered with a significant number of correct answers. The most common error was not deducting the cost of the machine when calculating the average profit.
notes.5b: Most candidates were able to state two disadvantages of the method but generally only one advantage.
notes.5c: This was very well answered with many candidates being awarded full marks. There were no common errors.
notes.5d: Most candidates did know the formula of IRR and were able to apply it.
notes.5e: Most candidates answered this for the advice and then provided acceptable justification to be awarded a further three or four marks. �PAGE�16
notes.5f: The calculation was challenging to most candidates with very few correct solutions.
notes.6a: Most candidates could state one disadvantage of operating a standard costing system with some able to state a second disadvantage.
notes.6b: Performance was mixed with candidates who had a good knowledge of variances scoring full marks. Nearly all were able to obtain the available mark for the total labour variance.
notes.6c: This was well answered with most candidates able to identify possible reasons for their calculated variances.
notes.6d: The reconciliation was answered to a reasonable standard with some fully correct statements. Common errors included the incorrect calculation of the standard material and labour costs and treating the variances in the wrong direction in the statement.
notes.6e: Most candidates provided the required advice and many then did justify their answer and were consequently awarded both of the available marks. �PAGE�17
notes.key_messages:
Candidates should focus on all sections of the syllabus and should read the question requirements carefully
before answering. Some candidates omitted calculations and did not get any marks where there was an
incorrect final value only.
notes.general_comments:
Overall performance of candidates was reasonable. Questions 1 and 5 were the best answered questions
on the paper.
